title: I Posted the Ham-Radio Shack Hours After They Camped My Key

parts.text: I stepped into shack A at 7:04 p.m. and trustee Glen was already using my numbered key. The board said: ONE HOUR. ONE KEY. LOG EVERY QSO. I was forty-two, club trustee, holding a clipboard that listed our net. Glen shrugged. "Trustees are the shack." I photographed the board, the booking, and his fist on my key. Then I asked for the shack hours. At 7:12 the net desk pinged why Glen's fist sat on our key. I kept my voice indoor and let the timestamp talk. A paper policy is only paper until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The net desk can see Glen's fist in shack A during our net.

social.video_title: He camped my numbered ham key — Part 1/2
social.description: Ham shack, a trustee on my key, a one-hour clock he posted. I logged the fist. Would you have asked for the shack hours?

parts.text: Glen called it tuning until the desk asked for the photo. I printed the ticket, the board, and the key still. The key went back to my numbered clip. Glen ran a slot of their own and told the next trustee atmosphere was always about optics. Optics is a word people use when a booking exists. Policy now has a second line: TRUSTEES ARE NOT THE SHACK. I keep our net on a labeled card. Glen brown-bags his fists. The shack finally looks like a booking, not a loan. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.video_title: Trustees are not the shack — Part 2/2
social.description: Shack hours, numbered key, and a second line on the board. Was tuning ever our net?
